import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Calculate effect sizes (mean difference in outcome)
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] == 'clinical':
            # For clinical features, use t-test statistic
            t_stat = feats.x[:, i].std() * np.sqrt(feats.n) * (feats.x[feats.y==1, i].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0, i].mean()) / feats.x[:, i].std()
            effect_sizes.append(abs(t_stat))
        else:
            # For other features, use mean difference directly
            effect_sizes.append(abs(feats.x[feats.y==1, i].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0, i].mean()))
    
    # Sort by effect size
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1]
    
    # Select top features, avoiding near-duplicates
    selected_features = []
    used_ids = set()
    
    # Check correlations to avoid near-duplicates
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    corr_threshold = 0.6
    
    for idx in sorted_indices[:10]:  # Look at top 10
        fid = feats.ids[idx]
        # Check if this feature is correlated with any already selected
        is_duplicate = False
        for selected_fid in selected_features:
            selected_idx = feats.column(selected_fid)
            if abs(corr_matrix[idx, selected_idx]) >= corr_threshold:
                is_duplicate = True
                break
        
        if not is_duplicate:
            selected_features.append(fid)
            if len(selected_features) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
                break
    
    # If we have no strong effects, return empty design
    if not selected_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Create a simple logistic regression model to identify important features
    X_selected = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in selected_features]]
    
    # Use L1 regularization to select important features
    clf = LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear', random_state=42)
    clf.fit(X_selected, feats.y)
    
    # Get coefficients
    coef = clf.coef_[0]
    
    # Build final design
    drivers = tuple(selected_features[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    columns = tuple(selected_features)
    
    # Add interaction terms for top two features
    products = ()
    if len(selected_features) >= 2:
        products = ((selected_features[0], selected_features[1]),)
    
    # Loadings based on coefficient magnitudes
    loadings = dict(zip(selected_features, coef))
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
